sections.title: Chapter 1: King Sudyumna Becomes a Woman

verses.devanagari: श्रीराजोवाच\\nमन्वन्तराणि सर्वाणि त्वयोक्तानि श्रुतानि मे\\nवीर्याण्यनन्तवीर्यस्य हरेस्तत्र कृतानि च ॥१॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rājovāca\\nmanvantarāṇi sarvāṇi\\ntvayoktāni śrutāni me\\nvīryāṇy ananta-vīryasya\\nhares tatra kṛtāni ca
verses.translation: King Parīkṣit said: My lord, Śukadeva Gosvāmī, you have elaborately described all the periods of the various Manus and, within those periods, the wonderful activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has unlimited potency. I am fortunate to have heard all of this from you.

verses.devanagari: योऽसौ सत्यव्रतो नाम राजर्षिर्द्रविडेश्वरः\\nज्ञआनं योऽतीतकल्पान्ते लेभे पुरुषसेवया ॥२॥\\nस वै विवस्वतः पुत्रो मनुरासीदिति श्रुतम\\nत्वत्तस्तस्य सुताः प्रोक्ता इक्ष्वाकुप्रमुखा नृपाः ॥३॥
verses.transliteration: sa vai vivasvataḥ putro\\nmanur āsīd iti śrutam\\ntvattas tasya sutāḥ proktā\\nikṣvāku-pramukhā nṛpāḥ
verses.translation: Satyavrata, the saintly king of Draviḍadeśa who received spiritual knowledge at the end of the last millennium by the grace of the Supreme, later became Vaivasvata Manu, the son of Vivasvān, in the next manvantara [period of Manu]. I have received this knowledge from you. I also understand that such kings as Ikṣvāku were his sons, as you have already explained.

verses.devanagari: तेषां वंशं पृथग्ब्रह्मन्वंशानुचरितानि च\\nकीर्तयस्व महाभाग नित्यं शुश्रूषतां हि नः ॥४॥
verses.transliteration: teṣāṁ vaṁśaṁ pṛthag brahman\\nvaṁśānucaritāni ca\\nkīrtayasva mahā-bhāga\\nnityaṁ śuśrūṣatāṁ hi naḥ
verses.translation: O greatly fortunate Śukadeva Gosvāmī, O great brāhmaṇa, kindly describe to us separately the dynasties and characteristics of all those kings, for we are always eager to hear such topics from you.

verses.devanagari: ये भूता ये भविष्याश्च भवन्त्यद्यतनाश्च ये\\nतेषां नः पुण्यकीर्तीनां सर्वेषां वद विक्रमान ॥५॥
verses.transliteration: ye bhūtā ye bhaviṣyāś ca\\nbhavanty adyatanāś ca ye\\nteṣāṁ naḥ puṇya-kīrtīnāṁ\\nsarveṣāṁ vada vikramān
verses.translation: Kindly tell us about the abilities of all the celebrated kings born in the dynasty of Vaivasvata Manu, including those who have already passed, those who may appear in the future, and those who exist at present.

verses.devanagari: श्रीसूत उवाच\\nएवं परीक्षिता राज्ञआ सदसि ब्रह्मवादिनाम\\nपृष्टः प्रोवाच भगवाञ्छुकः परमधर्मवित ॥६॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-sūta uvāca\\nevaṁ parīkṣitā rājñā\\nsadasi brahma-vādinām\\npṛṣṭaḥ provāca bhagavāñ\\nchukaḥ parama-dharma-vit
verses.translation: Sūta Gosvāmī said: When Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the greatest knower of religious principles, was thus requested by Mahārāja Parīkṣit in the assembly of all the scholars learned in Vedic knowledge, he then proceeded to speak.

verses.devanagari: श्रीशुक उवाच\\nश्रूयतां मानवो वंशः प्राचुर्येण परन्तप\\nन शक्यते विस्तरतो वक्तुं वर्षशतैरपि ॥७॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-śuka uvāca\\nśrūyatāṁ mānavo vaṁśaḥ\\nprācuryeṇa parantapa\\nna śakyate vistarato\\nvaktuṁ varṣa-śatair api
verses.translation: Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: O King, subduer of your enemies, now hear from me in great detail about the dynasty of Manu. I shall explain as much as possible, although one could not say everything about it, even in hundreds of years.

verses.devanagari: परावरेषां भूतानामात्मा यः पुरुषः परः\\nस एवासीदिदं विश्वं कल्पान्तेऽन्यन्न किञ्चन ॥८॥
verses.transliteration: parāvareṣāṁ bhūtānām\\nātmā yaḥ puruṣaḥ paraḥ\\nsa evāsīd idaṁ viśvaṁ\\nkalpānte 'nyan na kiñcana
verses.translation: The transcendental Supreme Person, the Supersoul of all living entities, who are in different statuses of life, high and low, existed at the end of the millennium, when neither this manifested cosmos nor anything else but Him existed.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nTaking the proper position from which to describe the dynasty of Manu, Śukadeva Gosvāmī begins by saying that when the entire world is inundated, only the Supreme Personality of Godhead exists, and nothing else. Śukadeva Gosvāmī will now describe how the Lord creates other things, one after another.

verses.devanagari: तस्य नाभेः समभवत्पद्मकोषो हिरण्मयः\\nतस्मिन्जज्ञए महाराज स्वयम्भूश्चतुराननः ॥९॥
verses.transliteration: tasya nābheḥ samabhavat\\npadma-koṣo hiraṇmayaḥ\\ntasmiñ jajñe mahārāja\\nsvayambhūś catur-ānanaḥ
verses.translation: O King Parīkṣit, from the navel of the Supreme Personality of Godhead was generated a golden lotus, on which the four-faced Lord Brahmā took his birth.

verses.devanagari: मरीचिर्मनसस्तस्य जज्ञए तस्यापि कश्यपः\\nदाक्षायण्यां ततोऽदित्यां विवस्वानभवत्सुतः ॥१०॥
verses.transliteration: marīcir manasas tasya\\njajñe tasyāpi kaśyapaḥ\\ndākṣāyaṇyāṁ tato 'dityāṁ\\nvivasvān abhavat sutaḥ
verses.translation: From the mind of Lord Brahmā, Marīci took birth, and from the semen of Marīci, Kaśyapa appeared from the womb of the daughter of Dakṣa Mahārāja. From Kaśyapa, by the womb of Aditi, Vivasvān took birth.

verses.devanagari: ततो मनुः श्राद्धदेवः संज्ञआयामास भारत\\nश्रद्धायां जनयामास दश पुत्रान्स आत्मवान ॥११॥\\nइक्ष्वाकुनृगशर्याति दिष्टधृष्टकरूषकान\\nनरिष्यन्तं पृषध्रं च नभगं च कविं विभुः ॥१२॥
verses.transliteration: ikṣvāku-nṛga-śaryāti-\\ndiṣṭa-dhṛṣṭa-karūṣakān\\nnariṣyantaṁ pṛṣadhraṁ ca\\nnabhagaṁ ca kaviṁ vibhuḥ
verses.translation: O King, best of the Bhārata dynasty, from Vivasvān, by the womb of Saṁjñā, Śrāddhadeva Manu was born. Śrāddhadeva Manu, having conquered his senses, begot ten sons in the womb of his wife, Śraddhā. The names of these sons were Ikṣvāku, Nṛga, Śaryāti, Diṣṭa, Dhṛṣṭa, Karūṣaka, Nariṣyanta, Pṛṣadhra, Nabhaga and Kavi.

verses.devanagari: अप्रजस्य मनोः पूर्वं वसिष्ठो भगवान्किल\\nमित्रावरुणयोरिष्टिं प्रजार्थमकरोद्विभुः ॥१३॥
verses.transliteration: aprajasya manoḥ pūrvaṁ\\nvasiṣṭho bhagavān kila\\nmitrā-varuṇayor iṣṭiṁ\\nprajārtham akarod vibhuḥ
verses.translation: Manu at first had no sons. Therefore, in order to get a son for him, the great saint Vasiṣṭha, who was very powerful in spiritual knowledge, performed a sacrifice to satisfy the demigods Mitra and Varuṇa.

verses.devanagari: तत्र श्रद्धा मनोः पत्नी होतारं समयाचत\\nदुहित्रर्थमुपागम्य प्रणिपत्य पयोव्रता ॥१४॥
verses.transliteration: tatra śraddhā manoḥ patnī\\nhotāraṁ samayācata\\nduhitrartham upāgamya\\npraṇipatya payovratā
verses.translation: During that sacrifice, Śraddhā, Manu's wife, who was observing the vow of subsisting only by drinking milk, approached the priest offering the sacrifice, offered obeisances to him and begged for a daughter.

verses.devanagari: प्रेषितोऽध्वर्युणा होता व्यचरत्तत्समाहितः\\nगृहीते हविषि वाचा वषट्कारं गृणन्द्विजः ॥१५॥
verses.transliteration: preṣito 'dhvaryuṇā hotā\\nvyacarat tat samāhitaḥ\\ngṛhīte haviṣi vācā\\nvaṣaṭ-kāraṁ gṛṇan dvijaḥ
verses.translation: Told by the chief priest "Now offer oblations," the person in charge of oblations took clarified butter to offer. He then remembered the request of Manu's wife and performed the sacrifice while chanting the word "vaṣaṭ."

verses.devanagari: होतुस्तद्व्यभिचारेण कन्येला नाम साभवत\\nतां विलोक्य मनुः प्राह नातितुष्टमना गुरुम ॥१६॥
verses.transliteration: hotus tad-vyabhicāreṇa\\nkanyelā nāma sābhavat\\ntāṁ vilokya manuḥ prāha\\nnātituṣṭamanā gurum
verses.translation: Manu had begun that sacrifice for the sake of getting a son, but because the priest was diverted by the request of Manu's wife, a daughter named Ilā was born. Upon seeing the daughter, Manu was not very satisfied. Thus he spoke to his guru, Vasiṣṭha, as follows.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nBecause Manu had no issue, he was pleased at the birth of the child, even though a daughter, and gave her the name Ilā. Later, however, he was not very satisfied to see the daughter instead of a son. Because he had no issue, he was certainly very glad at the birth of Ilā, but his pleasure was temporary.

verses.devanagari: भगवन्किमिदं जातं कर्म वो ब्रह्मवादिनाम\\nविपर्ययमहो कष्टं मैवं स्याद्ब्रह्मविक्रिया ॥१७॥
verses.transliteration: bhagavan kim idaṁ jātaṁ\\nkarma vo brahma-vādinām\\nviparyayam aho kaṣṭaṁ\\nmaivaṁ syād brahma-vikriyā
verses.translation: My lord, all of you are expert in chanting the Vedic mantras. How then has the result been opposite to the one desired? This is a matter for lamentation. There should not have been such a reversal of the results of the Vedic mantras.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In this age, the performance of
yajña
has been forbidden because no one can properly chant the Vedic
mantras.
If Vedic
mantras
are chanted properly, the desire for which a sacrifice is performed must be successful. Therefore the Hare Kṛṣṇa chant is called the
mahā-mantra,
the great, exalted
mantra
above all other Vedic
mantras,
because simply chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra
brings so many beneficial effects. As explained by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu (
Śikṣāṣṭaka
1):
ceto-darpaṇa-mārjanaṁ bhava-mahā-dāvāgni-nirvāpaṇaṁ
śreyaḥ-kairava-candrikā-vitaraṇaṁ vidyā-vadhū-jīvanam
ānandāmbudhi-vardhanaṁ prati-padaṁ pūrṇāmṛtāsvādanaṁ
sarvātma-snapanaṁ paraṁ vijayate śrī-kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtanam
[[cc/antya/20/12|[Cc. Antya 20.12] ]]
"Glory to the Śrī Kṛṣṇa
saṅkīrtana,
which cleanses the heart of all the dust accumulated for years and extinguishes the fire of conditional life, of repeated birth and death. This
saṅkīrtana
movement is the prime benediction for humanity at large because it spreads the rays of the benediction moon. It is the life of all transcendental knowledge. It increases the ocean of transcendental bliss, and it enables us to fully taste the nectar for which we are always anxious."
Therefore, the best performance of
yajña
given to us is the
saṅkīrtana-yajña. Yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtana-prāyair yajanti hi sumedhasaḥ
(SB 11.5.32). Those who are intelligent take advantage of the greatest
yajña
in this age by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra
in congregation. When the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mantra
is chanted by many men together, the chanting is called
saṅkīrtana,
and as a result of such a
yajña
there will be clouds in the sky (
yajñād bhavati parjanyaḥ
[[bg/3/14|[Bg. 3.14] ]]). In these days of drought, people can gain relief from scarcity of rain and food by the simple method of the Hare Kṛṣṇa
yajña.
Indeed, this can relieve all of human society. At present there are droughts throughout Europe and America, and people are suffering, but if people take this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement seriously, if they stop their sinful activities and chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra,
all their problems will be solved without difficulty. In other processes of
yajña
there are difficulties because there are no learned scholars who can chant the
mantras
perfectly well, nor is it possible to secure the ingredients to perform the
yajña.
Because human society is poverty-stricken and men are devoid of Vedic knowledge and the power to chant the Vedic
mantras,
the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra
is the only shelter. People should be intelligent enough to chant it.
Yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtana-prāyair yajanti hi sumedhasaḥ
[SB 11.5.32]. Those whose brains are dull cannot understand this chanting, nor can they take to it.

verses.devanagari: यूयं ब्रह्मविदो युक्तास्तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषाः\\nकुतः सङ्कल्पवैषम्यमनृतं विबुधेष्विव ॥१८॥
verses.transliteration: yūyaṁ brahma-vido yuktās\\ntapasā dagdha-kilbiṣāḥ\\nkutaḥ saṅkalpa-vaiṣamyam\\nanṛtaṁ vibudheṣv iva
verses.translation: You are all self-controlled, well balanced in mind, and aware of the Absolute Truth. And because of austerities and penances you are completely cleansed of all material contamination. Your words, like those of the demigods, are never baffled. Then how is it possible that your determination has failed?
verses.purport: PURPORT\nWe have learned from many Vedic literatures that a benediction or curse given by the demigods never proves false. By performing austerities and penances, by controlling the senses and mind, and by achieving full knowledge of the Absolute Truth, one is fully cleansed of material contamination. Then one's words and blessings, like those of the demigods, are never a failure.

verses.devanagari: निशम्य तद्वचस्तस्य भगवान्प्रपितामहः\\nहोतुर्व्यतिक्रमं ज्ञआत्वा बभाषे रविनन्दनम ॥१९॥
verses.transliteration: niśamya tad vacas tasya\\nbhagavān prapitāmahaḥ\\nhotur vyatikramaṁ jñātvā\\nbabhāṣe ravi-nandanam
verses.translation: The most powerful great-grandfather Vasiṣṭha, after hearing these words of Manu, understood the discrepancy on the part of the priest. Thus he spoke as follows to the son of the sun-god.

verses.devanagari: एतत्सङ्कल्पवैषम्यं होतुस्ते व्यभिचारतः\\nतथापि साधयिष्ये ते सुप्रजास्त्वं स्वतेजसा ॥२०॥
verses.transliteration: etat saṅkalpa-vaiṣamyaṁ\\nhotus te vyabhicārataḥ\\ntathāpi sādhayiṣye te\\nsuprajāstvaṁ sva-tejasā
verses.translation: This discrepancy in the objective is due to your priest's deviation from the original purpose. However, by my own prowess I shall give you a good son.

verses.devanagari: एवं व्यवसितो राजन्भगवान्स महायशाः\\nअस्तौषीदादिपुरुषमिलायाः पुंस्त्वकाम्यया ॥२१॥
verses.transliteration: evaṁ vyavasito rājan\\nbhagavān sa mahā-yaśāḥ\\nastauṣīd ādi-puruṣam\\nilāyāḥ puṁstva-kāmyayā
verses.translation: Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King Parīkṣit, after the most famous and powerful Vasiṣṭha made this decision, he offered prayers to the Supreme Person, Viṣṇu, to transform Ilā into a male.

verses.devanagari: तस्मै कामवरं तुष्टो भगवान्हरिरीश्वरः\\nददाविलाभवत्तेन सुद्युम्नः पुरुषर्षभः ॥२२॥
verses.transliteration: tasmai kāma-varaṁ tuṣṭo\\nbhagavān harir īśvaraḥ\\ndadāv ilābhavat tena\\nsudyumnaḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
verses.translation: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, the supreme controller, being pleased with Vasiṣṭha, gave him the benediction he desired. Thus Ilā was transformed into a very fine male named Sudyumna.

verses.devanagari: स एकदा महाराज विचरन्मृगयां वने\\nवृतः कतिपयामात्यैरश्वमारुह्य सैन्धवम ॥२३॥\\nप्रगृह्य रुचिरं चापं शरांश्च परमाद्भुतान\\nदंशितोऽनुमृगं वीरो जगाम दिशमुत्तराम ॥२४॥
verses.transliteration: pragṛhya ruciraṁ cāpaṁ\\nśarāṁś ca paramādbhutān\\ndaṁśito 'numṛgaṁ vīro\\njagāma diśam uttarām
verses.translation: O King Parīkṣit, that hero Sudyumna, accompanied by a few ministers and associates and riding on a horse brought from Sindhupradeśa, once went into the forest to hunt. He wore armor and was decorated with bows and arrows, and he was very beautiful. While following the animals and killing them, he reached the northern part of the forest.

verses.devanagari: सुकुमारवनं मेरोरधस्तात्प्रविवेश ह\\nयत्रास्ते भगवान्छर्वो रममाणः सहोमया ॥२५॥
verses.transliteration: sukumāra-vanaṁ meror\\nadhastāt praviveśa ha\\nyatrāste bhagavāñ charvo\\nramamāṇaḥ sahomayā
verses.translation: There in the north, at the bottom of Mount Meru, is a forest known as Sukumāra where Lord Śiva always enjoys with Umā. Sudyumna entered that forest.

verses.devanagari: तस्मिन्प्रविष्ट एवासौ सुद्युम्नः परवीरहा\\nअपश्यत्स्त्रियमात्मानमश्वं च वडवां नृप ॥२६॥
verses.transliteration: tasmin praviṣṭa evāsau\\nsudyumnaḥ para-vīra-hā\\napaśyat striyam ātmānam\\naśvaṁ ca vaḍavāṁ nṛpa
verses.translation: O King Parīkṣit, as soon as Sudyumna, who was expert in subduing enemies, entered the forest, he saw himself transformed into a female and his horse transformed into a mare.

verses.devanagari: तथा तदनुगाः सर्वे आत्मलिङ्गविपर्ययम\\nदृष्ट्वा विमनसोऽभूवन्वीक्षमाणाः परस्परम ॥२७॥
verses.transliteration: tathā tad-anugāḥ sarve\\nātma-liṅga-viparyayam\\ndṛṣṭvā vimanaso 'bhūvan\\nvīkṣamāṇāḥ parasparam
verses.translation: When his followers also saw their identities transformed and their sex reversed, they were all very morose and just looked at one another.

verses.devanagari: श्रीराजोवाच\\nकथमेवं गुणो देशः केन वा भगवन्कृतः\\nप्रश्नमेनं समाचक्ष्व परं कौतूहलं हि नः ॥२८॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rājovāca\\nkatham evaṁ guṇo deśaḥ\\nkena vā bhagavan kṛtaḥ\\npraśnam enaṁ samācakṣva\\nparaṁ kautūhalaṁ hi naḥ
verses.translation: Mahārāja Parīkṣit said: O most powerful brāhmaṇa, why was this place so empowered, and who made it so powerful? Kindly answer this question, for I am very eager to hear about this.

verses.devanagari: श्रीशुक उवाच\\nएकदा गिरिशं द्रष्टुमृषयस्तत्र सुव्रताः\\nदिशो वितिमिराभासाः कुर्वन्तः समुपागमन ॥२९॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-śuka uvāca\\nekadā giriśaṁ draṣṭum\\nṛṣayas tatra suvratāḥ\\ndiśo vitimirābhāsāḥ\\nkurvantaḥ samupāgaman
verses.translation: Śukadeva Gosvāmī answered: Great saintly persons who strictly observed the spiritual rules and regulations and whose own effulgence dissipated all the darkness of all directions once came to see Lord Śiva in that forest.

verses.devanagari: तान्विलोक्याम्बिका देवी विवासा व्रीडिता भृशम\\nभर्तुरङ्कात्समुत्थाय नीवीमाश्वथ पर्यधात ॥३०॥
verses.transliteration: tān vilokyāmbikā devī\\nvivāsā vrīḍitā bhṛśam\\nbhartur aṅkāt samutthāya\\nnīvīm āśv atha paryadhāt
verses.translation: When the goddess Ambikā saw the great saintly persons, she was very much ashamed because at that time she was naked. She immediately got up from the lap of her husband and tried to cover her breast.

verses.devanagari: ऋषयोऽपि तयोर्वीक्ष्य प्रसङ्गं रममाणयोः\\nनिवृत्ताः प्रययुस्तस्मान्नरनारायणाश्रमम ॥३१॥
verses.transliteration: ṛṣayo 'pi tayor vīkṣya\\nprasaṅgaṁ ramamāṇayoḥ\\nnivṛttāḥ prayayus tasmān\\nnara-nārāyaṇāśramam
verses.translation: Seeing Lord Śiva and Pārvatī engaged in sexual affairs, all the great saintly persons immediately desisted from going further and departed for the āśrama of Nara-Nārāyaṇa.

verses.devanagari: तदिदं भगवानाह प्रियायाः प्रियकाम्यया\\nस्थानं यः प्रविशेदेतत्स वै योषिद्भवेदिति ॥३२॥
verses.transliteration: tad idaṁ bhagavān āha\\npriyāyāḥ priya-kāmyayā\\nsthānaṁ yaḥ praviśed etat\\nsa vai yoṣid bhaved iti
verses.translation: Thereupon, just to please his wife, Lord Śiva said, "Any male entering this place shall immediately become a female!"

verses.devanagari: तत ऊर्ध्वं वनं तद्वै पुरुषा वर्जयन्ति हि\\nसा चानुचरसंयुक्ता विचचार वनाद्वनम ॥३३॥
verses.transliteration: tata ūrdhvaṁ vanaṁ tad vai\\npuruṣā varjayanti hi\\nsā cānucara-saṁyuktā\\nvicacāra vanād vanam
verses.translation: Since that time, no male had entered that forest. But now King Sudyumna, having been transformed into a female, began to walk with his associates from one forest to another.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In
Bhagavad-gītā
(Bg. 2.22) it is said:
vāsāṁsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya
navāni gṛhṇāti naro 'parāṇi
tathā sarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny
anyāni saṁyāti navāni dehī
"As a person puts on new garments, giving up old ones, the soul accepts new material bodies, giving up the old and useless ones."
The body is just like a dress, and here this is proved. Sudyumna and his associates were all male, which means that their souls were covered by male dress, but now they became female, which means that their dress was changed. The soul, however, remains the same. It is said that by modern medical treatment a male can be transformed into a female, and a female into a male. The body, however, has no connection with the soul. The body can be changed, either in this life or the next. Therefore, one who has knowledge of the soul and how the soul transmigrates from one body to another does not pay attention to the body, which is nothing but a covering dress.
Paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśinaḥ
[[bg/5/18|[Bg. 5.18] ]]. Such a person sees the soul, which is part and parcel of the Supreme Lord. Therefore he is a
sama-darśi,
a learned person.

verses.devanagari: अथ तामाश्रमाभ्याशे चरन्तीं प्रमदोत्तमाम\\nस्त्रीभिः परिवृतां वीक्ष्य चकमे भगवान्बुधः ॥३४॥
verses.transliteration: atha tām āśramābhyāśe\\ncarantīṁ pramadottamām\\nstrībhiḥ parivṛtāṁ vīkṣya\\ncakame bhagavān budhaḥ
verses.translation: Sudyumna had been transformed into the best of beautiful women who excite sexual desire and was surrounded by other women. Upon seeing this beautiful woman loitering near his āśrama, Budha, the son of the moon, immediately desired to enjoy her.

verses.devanagari: सापि तं चकमे सुभ्रूः सोमराजसुतं पतिम\\nस तस्यां जनयामास पुरूरवसमात्मजम ॥३५॥
verses.transliteration: sāpi taṁ cakame subhrūḥ\\nsomarāja-sutaṁ patim\\nsa tasyāṁ janayām āsa\\npurūravasam ātmajam
verses.translation: The beautiful woman also desired to accept Budha, the son of the king of the moon, as her husband. Thus Budha begot in her womb a son named Purūravā.

verses.devanagari: एवं स्त्रीत्वमनुप्राप्तः सुद्युम्नो मानवो नृपः\\nसस्मार स कुलाचार्यं वसिष्ठमिति शुश्रुम ॥३६॥
verses.transliteration: evaṁ strītvam anuprāptaḥ\\nsudyumno mānavo nṛpaḥ\\nsasmāra sa kulācāryaṁ\\nvasiṣṭham iti śuśruma
verses.translation: I heard from reliable sources that King Sudyumna, the son of Manu, having thus achieved femininity, remembered his familial spiritual master, Vasiṣṭha.

verses.devanagari: स तस्य तां दशां दृष्ट्वा कृपया भृशपीडितः\\nसुद्युम्नस्याशयन्पुंस्त्वमुपाधावत शङ्करम ॥३७॥
verses.transliteration: sa tasya tāṁ daśāṁ dṛṣṭvā\\nkṛpayā bhṛśa-pīḍitaḥ\\nsudyumnasyāśayan puṁstvam\\nupādhāvata śaṅkaram
verses.translation: Upon seeing Sudyumna's deplorable condition, Vasiṣṭha was very much aggrieved. Desiring for Sudyumna to regain his maleness, Vasiṣṭha again began to worship Lord Śaṅkara [Śiva].

verses.devanagari: तुष्टस्तस्मै स भगवानृषये प्रियमावहन\\nस्वां च वाचमृतां कुर्वन्निदमाह विशाम्पते ॥३८॥\\nमासं पुमान्स भविता मासं स्त्री तव गोत्रजः\\nइत्थं व्यवस्थया कामं सुद्युम्नोऽवतु मेदिनीम ॥३९॥
verses.transliteration: māsaṁ pumān sa bhavitā\\nmāsaṁ strī tava gotrajaḥ\\nitthaṁ vyavasthayā kāmaṁ\\nsudyumno 'vatu medinīm
verses.translation: O King Parīkṣit, Lord Śiva was pleased with Vasiṣṭha. Therefore, to satisfy him and to keep his own word to Pārvatī, Lord Śiva said to that saintly person, "Your disciple Sudyumna may remain a male for one month and a female for the next. In this way he may rule the world as he likes."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The word
gotrajaḥ
is significant in this connection.
Brāhmaṇas
generally act as spiritual masters of two dynasties. One is their disciplic succession, and the other is the dynasty born of their semen. Both descendants belong to the same
gotra,
or dynasty. In the Vedic system we sometimes find that both
brāhmaṇas
and
kṣatriyas
and even
vaiśyas
come in the disciplic succession of the same
ṛṣis.
Because the
gotra
and dynasty are one, there is no difference between the disciples and the family born of the semen. The same system still prevails in Indian society, especially in regard to marriage, for which the
gotra
is calculated. Here the word
gotrajaḥ
refers to those born in the same dynasty, whether they be disciples or members of the family.

verses.devanagari: आचार्यानुग्रहात्कामं लब्ध्वा पुंस्त्वं व्यवस्थया\\nपालयामास जगतीं नाभ्यनन्दन्स्म तं प्रजाः ॥४०॥
verses.transliteration: ācāryānugrahāt kāmaṁ\\nlabdhvā puṁstvaṁ vyavasthayā\\npālayām āsa jagatīṁ\\nnābhyanandan sma taṁ prajāḥ
verses.translation: Thus being favored by the spiritual master, according to the words of Lord Śiva, Sudyumna regained his desired maleness every alternate month and in this way ruled the kingdom, although the citizens were not satisfied with this.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThe citizens could understand that the king was transformed into a female every alternate month and therefore could not discharge his royal duty. Consequently they were not very satisfied.

verses.devanagari: तस्योत्कलो गयो राजन्विमलश्च त्रयः सुताः\\nदक्षिणापथराजानो बभूवुर्धर्मवत्सलाः ॥४१॥
verses.transliteration: tasyotkalo gayo rājan\\nvimalaś ca trayaḥ sutāḥ\\ndakṣiṇā-patha-rājāno\\nbabhūvur dharma-vatsalāḥ
verses.translation: O King, Sudyumna had three very pious sons, named Utkala, Gaya and Vimala, who became the kings of the Dakṣiṇā-patha.

verses.devanagari: ततः परिणते काले प्रतिष्ठानपतिः प्रभुः\\nपुरूरवस उत्सृज्य गां पुत्राय गतो वनम ॥४२॥
verses.transliteration: tataḥ pariṇate kāle\\npratiṣṭhāna-patiḥ prabhuḥ\\npurūravasa utsṛjya\\ngāṁ putrāya gato vanam
verses.translation: Thereafter, when the time was ripe, when Sudyumna, the king of the world, was sufficiently old, he delivered the entire kingdom to his son Purūravā and entered the forest.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
According to the Vedic system, one within the institution of
varṇa
and
āśrama
must leave his family life after he reaches fifty years of age (
pañcāśad ūrdhvaṁ vanaṁ vrajet
). Thus Sudyumna followed the prescribed regulations of
varṇāśrama
by leaving the kingdom and going to the forest to complete his spiritual life.
Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports of the Ninth Canto, Sixth Chapter, of the
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,
entitled "King Sudyumna Becomes a Woman."

sections.title: Chapter 2: The Dynasties of the Sons of Manu

verses.devanagari: श्रीशुक उवाच\\nएवं गतेऽथ सुद्युम्ने मनुर्वैवस्वतः सुते\\nपुत्रकामस्तपस्तेपे यमुनायां शतं समाः ॥१॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-śuka uvāca\\nevaṁ gate 'tha sudyumne\\nmanur vaivasvataḥ sute\\nputra-kāmas tapas tepe\\nyamunāyāṁ śataṁ samāḥ
verses.translation: Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Thereafter, when his son Sudyumna had thus gone to the forest to accept the order of vānaprastha, Vaivasvata Manu [Śrāddhadeva], being desirous of getting more sons, performed severe austerities on the bank of the Yamunā for one hundred years.

verses.devanagari: ततोऽयजन्मनुर्देवमपत्यार्थं हरिं प्रभुम\\nइक्ष्वाकुपूर्वजान्पुत्रान्लेभे स्वसदृशान्दश ॥२॥
verses.transliteration: tato 'yajan manur devam\\napatyārthaṁ hariṁ prabhum\\nikṣvāku-pūrvajān putrān\\nlebhe sva-sadṛśān daśa
verses.translation: Then, because of this desire for sons, the Manu known as Śrāddhadeva worshiped the Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead, the Lord of the demigods. Thus he got ten sons exactly like himself. Among them all, Ikṣvāku was the eldest.

verses.devanagari: पृषध्रस्तु मनोः पुत्रो गोपालो गुरुणा कृतः\\nपालयामास गा यत्तो रात्र्यां वीरासनव्रतः ॥३॥
verses.transliteration: pṛṣadhras tu manoḥ putro\\ngo-pālo guruṇā kṛtaḥ\\npālayām āsa gā yatto\\nrātryāṁ vīrāsana-vrataḥ
verses.translation: Among these sons, Pṛṣadhra, following the order of his spiritual master, was engaged as a protector of cows. He would stand all night with a sword to give the cows protection.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
One who becomes
vīrāsana
takes the vow to stand all night with a sword to give protection to the cows. Because Pṛṣadhra was engaged in this way, it is to be understood that he had no dynasty. We can further understand from this vow accepted by Pṛṣadhra how essential it is to protect the cows. Some son of a
kṣatriya
would take this vow to protect the cows from ferocious animals, even at night. What then is to be said of sending cows to slaughterhouses? This is the most sinful activity in human society.

verses.devanagari: एकदा प्राविशद्गोष्ठं शार्दूलो निशि वर्षति\\nशयाना गाव उत्थाय भीतास्ता बभ्रमुर्व्रजे ॥४॥
verses.transliteration: ekadā prāviśad goṣṭhaṁ\\nśārdūlo niśi varṣati\\nśayānā gāva utthāya\\nbhītās tā babhramur vraje
verses.translation: Once at night, while it was raining, a tiger entered the land of the cowshed. Upon seeing the tiger, all the cows, who were lying down, got up in fear and scattered here and there on the land.

verses.devanagari: एकां जग्राह बलवान्सा चुक्रोश भयातुरा\\nतस्यास्तु क्रन्दितं श्रुत्वा पृषध्रोऽनुससार ह ॥५॥\\nखड्गमादाय तरसा प्रलीनोडुगणे निशि\\nअजानन्नच्छिनोद्बभ्रोः शिरः शार्दूलशङ्कया ॥६॥
verses.transliteration: khaḍgam ādāya tarasā\\npralīnoḍu-gaṇe niśi\\najānann acchinod babhroḥ\\nśiraḥ śārdūla-śaṅkayā
verses.translation: When the very strong tiger seized the cow, the cow screamed in distress and fear, and Pṛṣadhra, hearing the screaming, immediately followed the sound. He took up his sword, but because the stars were covered by clouds, he mistook the cow for the tiger and mistakenly cut off the cows' head with great force.

verses.devanagari: व्याघ्रोऽपि वृक्णश्रवणो निस्त्रिंशाग्राहतस्ततः\\nनिश्चक्राम भृशं भीतो रक्तं पथि समुत्सृजन ॥७॥
verses.transliteration: vyāghro 'pi vṛkṇa-śravaṇo\\nnistriṁśāgrāhatas tataḥ\\nniścakrāma bhṛśaṁ bhīto\\nraktaṁ pathi samutsṛjan
verses.translation: Because the tiger's ear had been cut by the edge of the sword, the tiger was very afraid, and it fled from that place, while bleeding on the street.

verses.devanagari: मन्यमानो हतं व्याघ्रं पृषध्रः परवीरहा\\nअद्राक्षीत्स्वहतां बभ्रुं व्युष्टायां निशि दुःखितः ॥८॥
verses.transliteration: manyamāno hataṁ vyāghraṁ\\npṛṣadhraḥ para-vīra-hā\\nadrākṣīt sva-hatāṁ babhruṁ\\nvyuṣṭāyāṁ niśi duḥkhitaḥ
verses.translation: In the morning, when Pṛṣadhra, who was quite able to subdue his enemy, saw that he had killed the cow although at night he thought he had killed the tiger, he was very unhappy.

verses.devanagari: तं शशाप कुलाचार्यः कृतागसमकामतः\\nन क्षत्रबन्धुः शूद्रस्त्वं कर्मणा भवितामुना ॥९॥
verses.transliteration: taṁ śaśāpa kulācāryaḥ\\nkṛtāgasam akāmataḥ\\nna kṣatra-bandhuḥ śūdras tvaṁ\\nkarmaṇā bhavitāmunā
verses.translation: Although Pṛṣadhra had committed the sin unknowingly, his family priest, Vasiṣṭha, cursed him, saying, "In your next life you shall not be able to become a kṣatriya. Instead, you shall take birth as a śūdra because of killing the cow."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
It appears that Vasiṣṭha was not free from
tamo-guṇa,
the mode of ignorance. As the family priest or spiritual master of Pṛṣadhra, Vasiṣṭha should have taken Pṛṣadhra's offense very lightly, but instead Vasiṣṭha cursed him to become a
śūdra.
It is the duty of a family priest not to curse a disciple but to give him relief through the performance of some sort of atonement. Vasiṣṭha, however, did just the opposite. Therefore Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura says that he was
durmati;
in other words, his intelligence was not very good.

verses.devanagari: एवं शप्तस्तु गुरुणा प्रत्यगृह्णात्कृताञ्जलिः\\nअधारयद्व्रतं वीर ऊर्ध्वरेता मुनिप्रियम ॥१०॥
verses.transliteration: evaṁ śaptas tu guruṇā\\npratyagṛhṇāt kṛtāñjaliḥ\\nadhārayad vrataṁ vīra\\nūrdhva-retā muni-priyam
verses.translation: When the hero Pṛṣadhra was thus cursed by his spiritual master, he accepted the curse with folded hands. Then, having controlled his senses, he took the vow of brahmacarya, which is approved by all great sages.

verses.devanagari: वासुदेवे भगवति सर्वात्मनि परेऽमले\\nएकान्तित्वं गतो भक्त्या सर्वभूतसुहृत्समः ॥११॥\\nविमुक्तसङ्गः शान्तात्मा संयताक्षोऽपरिग्रहः\\nयदृच्छयोपपन्नेन कल्पयन्वृत्तिमात्मनः ॥१२॥\\nआत्मन्यात्मानमाधाय ज्ञआनतृप्तः समाहितः\\nविचचार महीमेतां जडान्धबधिराकृतिः ॥१३॥
verses.transliteration: ātmany ātmānam ādhāya\\njñāna-tṛptaḥ samāhitaḥ\\nvicacāra mahīm etāṁ\\njaḍāndha-badhirākṛtiḥ
verses.translation: Thereafter, Pṛṣadhra gained relief from all responsibilities, became peaceful in mind, and established control over all his senses. Being unaffected by material conditions, being pleased with whatever was available by the grace of the Lord to maintain body and soul together, and being equal toward everyone, he gave full attention to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vāsudeva, who is the transcendental Supersoul, free from material contamination. Thus Pṛṣadhra, fully satisfied in pure knowledge, always keeping his mind on the Supreme Personality of Godhead, achieved pure devotional service to the Lord and began traveling all over the world, without affection for material activities, as if he were deaf, dumb and blind.

verses.devanagari: एवं वृत्तो वनं गत्वा दृष्ट्वा दावाग्निमुत्थितम\\nतेनोपयुक्तकरणो ब्रह्म प्राप परं मुनिः ॥१४॥
verses.transliteration: evaṁ vṛtto vanaṁ gatvā\\ndṛṣṭvā dāvāgnim utthitam\\ntenopayukta-karaṇo\\nbrahma prāpa paraṁ muniḥ
verses.translation: With this attitude, Pṛṣadhra became a great saint, and when he entered the forest and saw a blazing forest fire, he took this opportunity to burn his body in the fire. Thus he achieved the transcendental, spiritual world.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The Lord says in
Bhagavad-gītā
(Bg. 4.9):
janma karma ca me divyam
evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ
tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma
naiti mām eti so 'rjuna
"One who knows the transcendental nature of My appearance and activities does not, upon leaving the body, take his birth again in this material world, but attains My eternal abode, O Arjuna." Pṛṣadhra, because of his
karma,
was cursed to take his next birth as a
śūdra,
but because he took to saintly life, specifically concentrating his mind always upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he became a pure devotee. Immediately after giving up his body in the fire, he reached the spiritual world, as mentioned in
Bhagavad-gītā
(
mām eti
), as a result of his devotional situation. Devotional service performed by thinking of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is so powerful that although Pṛṣadhra was cursed he avoided the terrible consequence of becoming a
śūdra
and instead returned home, back to Godhead. As stated in
Brahma-saṁhitā
(5.54):
yas tv indra-gopam athavendram aho sva-karma-
bandhānurūpa-phala-bhājanam ātanoti
karmāṇi nirdahati kintu ca bhakti-bhājāṁ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
Those who engage in devotional service are unaffected by the results of their material activities. Otherwise, everyone, from the smallest microbe up to the King of heaven, Indra, is subject to the laws of
karma.
A pure devotee, being always engaged in the service of the Lord, is exempt from these laws.

verses.devanagari: कविः कनीयान्विषयेषु निःस्पृहो विसृज्य राज्यं सह बन्धुभिर्वनम\\nनिवेश्य चित्ते पुरुषं स्वरोचिषं विवेश कैशोरवयाः परं गतः ॥१५॥
verses.transliteration: kaviḥ kanīyān viṣayeṣu niḥspṛho\\nvisṛjya rājyaṁ saha bandhubhir vanam\\nniveśya citte puruṣaṁ sva-rociṣaṁ\\nviveśa kaiśora-vayāḥ paraṁ gataḥ
verses.translation: Being reluctant to accept material enjoyment, Manu's youngest son, whose name was Kavi, gave up the kingdom before attaining full youth. Accompanied by his friends, he went to the forest, always thinking of the self-effulgent Supreme Personality of Godhead within the core of his heart. Thus he attained perfection.

verses.devanagari: करूषान्मानवादासन्कारूषाः क्षत्रजातयः\\nउत्तरापथगोप्तारो ब्रह्मण्या धर्मवत्सलाः ॥१६॥
verses.transliteration: karūṣān mānavād āsan\\nkārūṣāḥ kṣatra-jātayaḥ\\nuttarā-patha-goptāro\\nbrahmaṇyā dharma-vatsalāḥ
verses.translation: From Karūṣa, another son of Manu, came the Kārūṣa dynasty, a family of kṣatriyas. The Kārūṣa kṣatriyas were the kings of the northern direction. They were celebrated protectors of brahminical culture and were all firmly religious.

verses.devanagari: धृष्टाद्धार्ष्टमभूत्क्षत्रं ब्रह्मभूयं गतं क्षितौ\\nनृगस्य वंशः सुमतिर्भूतज्योतिस्ततो वसुः ॥१७॥
verses.transliteration: dhṛṣṭād dhārṣṭam abhūt kṣatraṁ\\nbrahma-bhūyaṁ gataṁ kṣitau\\nnṛgasya vaṁśaḥ sumatir\\nbhūtajyotis tato vasuḥ
verses.translation: From the son of Manu named Dhṛṣṭa came a kṣatriya caste called Dhārṣṭa, whose members achieved the position of brāhmaṇas in this world. Then, from the son of Manu named Nṛga came Sumati. From Sumati came Bhūtajyoti, and from Bhūtajyoti came Vasu.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Here it is said,
kṣatraṁ brahma-bhūyaṁ gataṁ kṣitau:
although the Dhārṣṭas belonged to the
kṣatriya
caste, they were able to convert themselves into
brāhmaṇas.
This gives clear evidence supporting the following statement by Nārada (SB 7.11.35):
yasya yal lakṣaṇaṁ proktaṁ
puṁso varṇābhivyañjakam
yad anyatrāpi dṛśyeta
tat tenaiva vinirdiśet
If the qualities of one group are found in the men of another, those men should be recognized by their qualities, by their symptoms, not by the caste of the family in which they were born. Birth is not at all important; it is one's qualities that are stressed in all Vedic literature.

verses.devanagari: वसोः प्रतीकस्तत्पुत्र ओघवानोघवत्पिता\\nकन्या चौघवती नाम सुदर्शन उवाह ताम ॥१८॥
verses.transliteration: vasoḥ pratīkas tat-putra\\noghavān oghavat-pitā\\nkanyā caughavatī nāma\\nsudarśana uvāha tām
verses.translation: The son of Vasu was Pratīka, whose son was Oghavān. Oghavān's son was also known as Oghavān, and his daughter was Oghavatī. Sudarśana married that daughter.

verses.devanagari: चित्रसेनो नरिष्यन्तादृक्षस्तस्य सुतोऽभवत\\nतस्य मीढ्वांस्ततः पूर्ण इन्द्रसेनस्तु तत्सुतः ॥१९॥
verses.transliteration: citraseno nariṣyantād\\nṛkṣas tasya suto 'bhavat\\ntasya mīḍhvāṁs tataḥ pūrṇa\\nindrasenas tu tat-sutaḥ
verses.translation: From Nariṣyanta came a son named Citrasena and from him a son named Ṛkṣa. From Ṛkṣa came Mīḍhvān, from Mīḍhvān came Pūrṇa, and from Pūrṇa came Indrasena.

verses.devanagari: वीतिहोत्रस्त्विन्द्रसेनात्तस्य सत्यश्रवा अभूत\\nउरुश्रवाः सुतस्तस्य देवदत्तस्ततोऽभवत ॥२०॥
verses.transliteration: vītihotras tv indrasenāt\\ntasya satyaśravā abhūt\\nuruśravāḥ sutas tasya\\ndevadattas tato 'bhavat
verses.translation: From Indrasena came Vītihotra, from Vītihotra came Satyaśravā, from Satyaśravā came the son named Uruśravā, and from Uruśravā came Devadatta.

verses.devanagari: ततोऽग्निवेश्यो भगवानग्निः स्वयमभूत्सुतः\\nकानीन इति विख्यातो जातूकर्ण्यो महानृषिः ॥२१॥
verses.transliteration: tato 'gniveśyo bhagavān\\nagniḥ svayam abhūt sutaḥ\\nkānīna iti vikhyāto\\njātūkarṇyo mahān ṛṣiḥ
verses.translation: From Devadatta came a son known as Agniveśya, who was the fire-god Agni himself. This son, who was a celebrated saint, was well known as Kānīna and Jātūkarṇya.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nAgniveśya was also known as Kānīna and Jātūkarṇya.

verses.devanagari: ततो ब्रह्मकुलं जातमाग्निवेश्यायनं नृप\\nनरिष्यन्तान्वयः प्रोक्तो दिष्टवंशमतः शृणु ॥२२॥
verses.transliteration: tato brahma-kulaṁ jātam\\nāgniveśyāyanaṁ nṛpa\\nnariṣyantānvayaḥ prokto\\ndiṣṭa-vaṁśam ataḥ śṛṇu
verses.translation: O King, from Agniveśya came a brahminical dynasty known as Āgniveśyāyana. Now that I have described the descendants of Nariṣyanta, let me describe the descendants of Diṣṭa. Please hear from me.

verses.devanagari: नाभागो दिष्टपुत्रोऽन्यः कर्मणा वैश्यतां गतः\\nभलन्दनः सुतस्तस्य वत्सप्रीतिर्भलन्दनात ॥२३॥\\nवत्सप्रीतेः सुतः प्रांशुस्तत्सुतं प्रमतिं विदुः\\nखनित्रः प्रमतेस्तस्माच्चाक्षुषोऽथ विविंशतिः ॥२४॥
verses.transliteration: vatsaprīteḥ sutaḥ prāṁśus\\ntat-sutaṁ pramatiṁ viduḥ\\nkhanitraḥ pramates tasmāc\\ncākṣuṣo 'tha viviṁśatiḥ
verses.translation: Diṣṭa had a son by the name Nābhāga. This Nābhāga, who was different from the Nābhāga described later, became a vaiśya by occupational duty. The son of Nābhāga was known as Bhalandana, the son of Bhalandana was Vatsaprīti, and his son was Prāṁśu. Prāṁśu's son was Pramati, Pramati's son was Khanitra, Khanitra's son was Cākṣuṣa, and his son was Viviṁśati.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
From Manu, one son became a
kṣatriya,
another a
brāhmaṇa,
and another a
vaiśya.
This confirms the statement by Nārada Muni,
yasya yal lakṣaṇaṁ proktaṁ puṁso varṇābhivyañjakam
(SB 7.11.35). One should always remember that
brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas
and
vaiśyas
should never be regarded as members of a caste by birth. A
brāhmaṇa
may be changed into a
kṣatriya,
and a
kṣatriya
into a
brāhmaṇa.
Similarly, a
brāhmaṇa
or
kṣatriya
may be changed into a
vaiśya,
and a
vaiśya
into a
brāhmaṇa
or
kṣatriya.
This is confirmed in
Bhagavad-gītā
(
cātur-varṇyaṁ mayā sṛṣṭaṁ guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśaḥ
[[bg/4/13|[Bg. 4.13] ]]). So one is a
brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya
or
vaiśya
never by birth, but by quality. There is a great need of
brāhmaṇas.
Therefore, in the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, we are trying to train some
brāhmaṇas
to guide human society. Because at present there is a scarcity of
brāhmaṇas,
the brain of human society is lost. Because practically everyone is a
śūdra,
no one at the present moment can guide the members of society to the proper path by which to achieve perfection in life.

verses.devanagari: विविंशतेः सुतो रम्भः खनीनेत्रोऽस्य धार्मिकः\\nकरन्धमो महाराज तस्यासीदात्मजो नृप ॥२५॥
verses.transliteration: viviṁśateḥ suto rambhaḥ\\nkhanīnetro 'sya dhārmikaḥ\\nkarandhamo mahārāja\\ntasyāsīd ātmajo nṛpa
verses.translation: The son of Viviṁśati was Rambha, whose son was the great and religious King Khanīnetra. O King, the son of Khanīnetra was King Karandhama.

verses.devanagari: तस्यावीक्षित्सुतो यस्य मरुत्तश्चक्रवर्त्यभूत\\nसंवर्तोऽयाजयद्यं वै महायोग्यङ्गिरःसुतः ॥२६॥
verses.transliteration: tasyāvīkṣit suto yasya\\nmaruttaś cakravarty abhūt\\nsaṁvarto 'yājayad yaṁ vai\\nmahā-yogy aṅgiraḥ-sutaḥ
verses.translation: From Karandhama came a son named Avīkṣit, and from Avīkṣit a son named Marutta, who was the emperor. The great mystic Saṁvarta, the son of Aṅgirā, engaged Marutta in performing a sacrifice [yajña].

verses.devanagari: मरुत्तस्य यथा यज्ञओ न तथान्योऽस्ति कश्चन\\nसर्वं हिरण्मयं त्वासीद्यत्किञ्चिच्चास्य शोभनम ॥२७॥
verses.transliteration: maruttasya yathā yajño\\nna tathānyo 'sti kaścana\\nsarvaṁ hiraṇmayaṁ tv āsīd\\nyat kiñcic cāsya śobhanam
verses.translation: The sacrificial paraphernalia of King Marutta was extremely beautiful, for everything was made of gold. Indeed, no other sacrifice could compare to his.

verses.devanagari: अमाद्यदिन्द्रः सोमेन दक्षिणाभिर्द्विजातयः\\nमरुतः परिवेष्टारो विश्वेदेवाः सभासदः ॥२८॥
verses.transliteration: amādyad indraḥ somena\\ndakṣiṇābhir dvijātayaḥ\\nmarutaḥ pariveṣṭāro\\nviśvedevāḥ sabhā-sadaḥ
verses.translation: In that sacrifice, King Indra became intoxicated by drinking a large quantity of soma-rasa. The brāhmaṇas received ample contributions, and therefore they were satisfied. For that sacrifice, the various demigods who control the winds offered foodstuffs, and the Viśvedevas were members of the assembly.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Because of the
yajña
performed by Marutta, everyone was pleased, especially the
brāhmaṇas
and
kṣatriyas. Brāhmaṇas
are interested in receiving contributions as priests, and
kṣatriyas
are interested in drinking. All of them, therefore, were satisfied with their different engagements.

verses.devanagari: मरुत्तस्य दमः पुत्रस्तस्यासीद्राज्यवर्धनः\\nसुधृतिस्तत्सुतो जज्ञए सौधृतेयो नरः सुतः ॥२९॥
verses.transliteration: maruttasya damaḥ putras\\ntasyāsīd rājyavardhanaḥ\\nsudhṛtis tat-suto jajñe\\nsaudhṛteyo naraḥ sutaḥ
verses.translation: Marutta's son was Dama, Dama's son was Rājyavardhana, Rājyavardhana's son was Sudhṛti, and his son was Nara.

verses.devanagari: तत्सुतः केवलस्तस्माद्धुन्धुमान्वेगवांस्ततः\\nबुधस्तस्याभवद्यस्य तृणबिन्दुर्महीपतिः ॥३०॥
verses.transliteration: tat-sutaḥ kevalas tasmād\\ndhundhumān vegavāṁs tataḥ\\nbudhas tasyābhavad yasya\\ntṛṇabindur mahīpatiḥ
verses.translation: The son of Nara was Kevala, and his son was Dhundhumān, whose son was Vegavān. Vegavān's son was Budha, and Budha's son was Tṛṇabindu, who became the king of this earth.

verses.devanagari: तं भेजेऽलम्बुषा देवी भजनीयगुणालयम\\nवराप्सरा यतः पुत्राः कन्या चेलविलाभवत ॥३१॥
verses.transliteration: taṁ bheje 'lambuṣā devī\\nbhajanīya-guṇālayam\\nvarāpsarā yataḥ putrāḥ\\nkanyā celavilābhavat
verses.translation: The best of the Apsarās, the highly qualified girl named Alambuṣā, accepted the similarly qualified Tṛṇabindu as her husband. She gave birth to a few sons and a daughter known as Ilavilā.

verses.devanagari: यस्यामुत्पादयामास विश्रवा धनदं सुतम\\nप्रादाय विद्यां परमामृषिर्योगेश्वरः पितुः ॥३२॥
verses.transliteration: yasyām utpādayām āsa\\nviśravā dhanadaṁ sutam\\nprādāya vidyāṁ paramām\\nṛṣir yogeśvaraḥ pituḥ
verses.translation: After the great saint Viśravā, the master of mystic yoga, received absolute knowledge from his father, he begot in the womb of Ilavilā the greatly celebrated son known as Kuvera, the giver of money.

verses.devanagari: विशालः शून्यबन्धुश्च धूम्रकेतुश्च तत्सुताः\\nविशालो वंशकृद्राजा वैशालीं निर्ममे पुरीम ॥३३॥
verses.transliteration: viśālaḥ śūnyabandhuś ca\\ndhūmraketuś ca tat-sutāḥ\\nviśālo vaṁśa-kṛd rājā\\nvaiśālīṁ nirmame purīm
verses.translation: Tṛṇabindu had three sons, named Viśāla, Śūnyabandhu and Dhūmraketu. Among these three, Viśāla created a dynasty and constructed a palace called Vaiśālī.

verses.devanagari: हेमचन्द्रः सुतस्तस्य धूम्राक्षस्तस्य चात्मजः\\nतत्पुत्रात्संयमादासीत्कृशाश्वः सहदेवजः ॥३४॥
verses.transliteration: hemacandraḥ sutas tasya\\ndhūmrākṣas tasya cātmajaḥ\\ntat-putrāt saṁyamād āsīt\\nkṛśāśvaḥ saha-devajaḥ
verses.translation: The son of Viśāla was known as Hemacandra, his son was Dhūmrākṣa, and his son was Saṁyama, whose sons were Devaja and Kṛśāśva.

verses.devanagari: कृशाश्वात्सोमदत्तोऽभूद्योऽश्वमेधैरिडस्पतिम\\nइष्ट्वा पुरुषमापाग्र्यां गतिं योगेश्वराश्रिताम ॥३५॥\\nसौमदत्तिस्तु सुमतिस्तत्पुत्रो जनमेजयः\\nएते वैशालभूपालास्तृणबिन्दोर्यशोधराः ॥३६॥
verses.transliteration: saumadattis tu sumatis\\ntat-putro janamejayaḥ\\nete vaiśāla-bhūpālās\\ntṛṇabindor yaśodharāḥ
verses.translation: The son of Kṛśāśva was Somadatta, who performed aśvamedha sacrifices and thus satisfied the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu. By worshiping the Supreme Lord, he achieved the most exalted post, a residence on the planet to which great mystic yogīs are elevated. The son of Somadatta was Sumati, whose son was Janamejaya. All these kings appearing in the dynasty of Viśāla properly maintained the celebrated position of King Tṛṇabindu.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports of the Ninth Canto, Second Chapter, of the
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,
entitled "The Dynasties of the Sons of Manu."

sections.title: Chapter 3: The Marriage of Sukanyā and Cyavana Muni

verses.devanagari: श्रीशुक उवाच\\nशर्यातिर्मानवो राजा ब्रह्मिष्ठः सम्बभूव ह\\nयो वा अङ्गिरसां सत्रे द्वितीयमहरूचिवान ॥१॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-śuka uvāca\\nśaryātir mānavo rājā\\nbrahmiṣṭhaḥ sambabhūva ha\\nyo vā aṅgirasāṁ satre\\ndvitīyam ahar ūcivān
verses.translation: Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: O King, Śaryāti, another son of Manu, was a ruler completely aware of Vedic knowledge. He gave instructions about the functions for the second day of the yajña to be performed by the descendants of Aṅgirā.

verses.devanagari: सुकन्या नाम तस्यासीत्कन्या कमललोचना\\nतया सार्धं वनगतो ह्यगमच्च्यवनाश्रमम ॥२॥
verses.transliteration: sukanyā nāma tasyāsīt\\nkanyā kamala-locanā\\ntayā sārdhaṁ vana-gato\\nhy agamac cyavanāśramam
verses.translation: Śaryāti had a beautiful lotus-eyed daughter named Sukanyā, with whom he went to the forest to see the āśrama of Cyavana Muni.

verses.devanagari: सा सखीभिः परिवृता विचिन्वन्त्यङ्घ्रिपान्वने\\nवल्मीकरन्ध्रे ददृशे खद्योते इव ज्योतिषी ॥३॥
verses.transliteration: sā sakhībhiḥ parivṛtā\\nvicinvanty aṅghripān vane\\nvalmīka-randhre dadṛśe\\nkhadyote iva jyotiṣī
verses.translation: While that Sukanyā, surrounded by her friends, was collecting various types of fruits from the trees in the forest, she saw within the hole of an earthworm two things glowing like luminaries.

verses.devanagari: ते दैवचोदिता बाला ज्योतिषी कण्टकेन वै\\nअविध्यन्मुग्धभावेन सुस्रावासृक्ततो बहिः ॥४॥
verses.transliteration: te daiva-coditā bālā\\njyotiṣī kaṇṭakena vai\\navidhyan mugdha-bhāvena\\nsusrāvāsṛk tato bahiḥ
verses.translation: As if induced by providence, the girl ignorantly pierced those two glowworms with a thorn, and when they were pierced, blood began to ooze out of them.

verses.devanagari: शकृन्मूत्रनिरोधोऽभूत्सैनिकानां च तत्क्षणात\\nराजर्षिस्तमुपालक्ष्य पुरुषान्विस्मितोऽब्रवीत ॥५॥
verses.transliteration: śakṛn-mūtra-nirodho 'bhūt\\nsainikānāṁ ca tat-kṣaṇāt\\nrājarṣis tam upālakṣya\\npuruṣān vismito 'bravīt
verses.translation: Thereupon, all the soldiers of Śaryāti were immediately obstructed from passing urine and stool. Upon perceiving this, Śaryāti spoke to his associates in surprise.

verses.devanagari: अप्यभद्रं न युष्माभिर्भार्गवस्य विचेष्टितम\\nव्यक्तं केनापि नस्तस्य कृतमाश्रमदूषणम ॥६॥
verses.transliteration: apy abhadraṁ na yuṣmābhir\\nbhārgavasya viceṣṭitam\\nvyaktaṁ kenāpi nas tasya\\nkṛtam āśrama-dūṣaṇam
verses.translation: How strange it is that one of us has attempted to do something wrong to Cyavana Muni, the son of Bhṛgu. It certainly appears that someone among us has polluted this āśrama.

verses.devanagari: सुकन्या प्राह पितरं भीता किञ्चित्कृतं मया\\nद्वे ज्योतिषी अजानन्त्या निर्भिन्ने कण्टकेन वै ॥७॥
verses.transliteration: sukanyā prāha pitaraṁ\\nbhītā kiñcit kṛtaṁ mayā\\ndve jyotiṣī ajānantyā\\nnirbhinne kaṇṭakena vai
verses.translation: Being very much afraid, the girl Sukanyā said to her father: I have done something wrong, for I have ignorantly pierced these two luminous substances with a thorn.

verses.devanagari: दुहितुस्तद्वचः श्रुत्वा शर्यातिर्जातसाध्वसः\\nमुनिं प्रसादयामास वल्मीकान्तर्हितं शनैः ॥८॥
verses.transliteration: duhitus tad vacaḥ śrutvā\\nśaryātir jāta-sādhvasaḥ\\nmuniṁ prasādayām āsa\\nvalmīkāntarhitaṁ śanaiḥ
verses.translation: After hearing this statement by his daughter, King Śaryāti was very much afraid. In various ways, he tried to appease Cyavana Muni, for it was he who sat within the hole of the earthworm.

verses.devanagari: तदभिप्रायमाज्ञआय प्रादाद्दुहितरं मुनेः\\nकृच्छ्रान्मुक्तस्तमामन्त्र्य पुरं प्रायात्समाहितः ॥९॥
verses.transliteration: tad-abhiprāyam ājñāya\\nprādād duhitaraṁ muneḥ\\nkṛcchrān muktas tam āmantrya\\npuraṁ prāyāt samāhitaḥ
verses.translation: King Śaryāti, being very contemplative and thus understanding Cyavana Muni's purpose, gave his daughter in charity to the sage. Thus released from danger with great difficulty, he took permission from Cyavana Muni and returned home.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The King, after hearing the statement of his daughter, certainly told the great sage Cyavana Muni everything about how his daughter had ignorantly committed such an offense. The
muni,
however, inquired from the King whether the daughter was married. In this way, the King, understanding the purpose of the great sage Cyavana Muni (
tad-abhiprāyam ājñāya
), immediately gave the
muni
his daughter in charity and escaped the danger of being cursed. Thus with the permission of the great sage the King returned home.

verses.devanagari: सुकन्या च्यवनं प्राप्य पतिं परमकोपनम\\nप्रीणयामास चित्तज्ञआ अप्रमत्तानुवृत्तिभिः ॥१०॥
verses.transliteration: sukanyā cyavanaṁ prāpya\\npatiṁ parama-kopanam\\nprīṇayām āsa citta-jñā\\napramattānuvṛttibhiḥ
verses.translation: Cyavana Muni was very irritable, but since Sukanyā had gotten him as her husband, she dealt with him carefully, according to his mood. Knowing his mind, she performed service to him without being bewildered.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is an indication of the relationship between husband and wife. A great personality like Cyavana Muni has the temperament of always wanting to be in a superior position. Such a person cannot submit to anyone. Therefore, Cyavana Muni had an irritable temperament. His wife, Sukanyā, could understand his attitude, and under the circumstances she treated him accordingly. If any wife wants to be happy with her husband, she must try to understand her husband's temperament and please him. This is victory for a woman. Even in the dealings of Lord Kṛṣṇa with His different queens, it has been seen that although the queens were the daughters of great kings, they placed themselves before Lord Kṛṣṇa as His maidservants. However great a woman may be, she must place herself before her husband in this way; that is to say, she must be ready to carry out her husband's orders and please him in all circumstances. Then her life will be successful. When the wife becomes as irritable as the husband, their life at home is sure to be disturbed or ultimately completely broken. In the modern day, the wife is never submissive, and therefore home life is broken even by slight incidents. Either the wife or the husband may take advantage of the divorce laws. According to the Vedic law, however, there is no such thing as divorce laws, and a woman must be trained to be submissive to the will of her husband. Westerners contend that this is a slave mentality for the wife, but factually it is not; it is the tactic by which a woman can conquer the heart of her husband, however irritable or cruel he may be. In this case we clearly see that although Cyavana Muni was not young but indeed old enough to be Sukanyā's grandfather and was also very irritable, Sukanyā, the beautiful young daughter of a king, submitted herself to her old husband and tried to please him in all respects. Thus she was a faithful and chaste wife.

verses.devanagari: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य नासत्यावाश्रमागतौ\\nतौ पूजयित्वा प्रोवाच वयो मे दत्तमीश्वरौ ॥११॥
verses.transliteration: kasyacit tv atha kālasya\\nnāsatyāv āśramāgatau\\ntau pūjayitvā provāca\\nvayo me dattam īśvarau
verses.translation: Thereafter, some time having passed, the Aśvinī-kumāra brothers, the heavenly physicians, happened to come to Cyavana Muni's āśrama. After offering them respectful obeisances, Cyavana Muni requested them to give him youthful life, for they were able to do so.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The heavenly physicians like the Aśvinī-kumāras could give youthful life even to one who was advanced in age. Indeed, great
yogīs,
with their mystic powers, can even bring a dead body back to life if the structure of the body is in order. We have already discussed this in connection with Bali Mahārāja's soldiers and their treatment by Śukrācārya. Modern medical science has not yet discovered how to bring a dead body back to life or bring youthful energy to an old body, but from these verses we can understand that such treatment is possible if one is able to take knowledge from the Vedic information. The Aśvinī-kumāras were expert in
Āyur-veda,
as was Dhanvantari. In every department of material science, there is a perfection to be achieved, and to achieve it one must consult the Vedic literature. The highest perfection is to become a devotee of the Lord. To attain this perfection, one must consult
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,
which is understood to be the ripe fruit of the Vedic desire tree (
nigama-kalpa-taror galitaṁ phalam
[[sb/1/1/3|[SB 1.1.3] ]]).

verses.devanagari: ग्रहं ग्रहीष्ये सोमस्य यज्ञए वामप्यसोमपोः\\nक्रियतां मे वयोरूपं प्रमदानां यदीप्सितम ॥१२॥
verses.transliteration: grahaṁ grahīṣye somasya\\nyajñe vām apy asoma-poḥ\\nkriyatāṁ me vayo-rūpaṁ\\npramadānāṁ yad īpsitam
verses.translation: Cyavana Muni said: Although you are ineligible to drink soma-rasa in sacrifices, I promise to give you a full pot of it. Kindly arrange beauty and youth for me, because they are attractive to young women.

verses.devanagari: बाढमित्यूचतुर्विप्रमभिनन्द्य भिषक्तमौ\\nनिमज्जतां भवानस्मिन्ह्रदे सिद्धविनिर्मिते ॥१३॥
verses.transliteration: bāḍham ity ūcatur vipram\\nabhinandya bhiṣaktamau\\nnimajjatāṁ bhavān asmin\\nhrade siddha-vinirmite
verses.translation: The great physicians, the Aśvinī-kumāras, very gladly accepted Cyavana Muni's proposal. Thus they told the brāhmaṇa, "Just dive into this lake of successful life." [One who bathes in this lake has his desires fulfilled.]

verses.devanagari: इत्युक्तो जरया ग्रस्त देहो धमनिसन्ततः\\nह्रदं प्रवेशितोऽश्विभ्यां वलीपलितविग्रहः ॥१४॥
verses.transliteration: ity ukto jarayā grasta-\\ndeho dhamani-santataḥ\\nhradaṁ praveśito 'śvibhyāṁ\\nvalī-palita-vigrahaḥ
verses.translation: After saying this, the Aśvinī-kumāras caught hold of Cyavana Muni, who was an old, diseased invalid with loose skin, white hair, and veins visible all over his body, and all three of them entered the lake.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nCyavana Muni was so old that he could not enter the lake alone. Thus the Aśvinī-kumāras caught hold of his body, and the three of them entered the lake.

verses.devanagari: पुरुषास्त्रय उत्तस्थुरपीव्या वनिताप्रियाः\\nपद्मस्रजः कुण्डलिनस्तुल्यरूपाः सुवाससः ॥१५॥
verses.transliteration: puruṣās traya uttasthur\\napīvyā vanitā-priyāḥ\\npadma-srajaḥ kuṇḍalinas\\ntulya-rūpāḥ suvāsasaḥ
verses.translation: Thereafter, three men with very beautiful bodily features emerged from the lake. They were nicely dressed and decorated with earrings and garlands of lotuses. All of them were of the same standard of beauty.

verses.devanagari: तान्निरीक्ष्य वरारोहा सरूपान्सूर्यवर्चसः\\nअजानती पतिं साध्वी अश्विनौ शरणं ययौ ॥१६॥
verses.transliteration: tān nirīkṣya varārohā\\nsarūpān sūrya-varcasaḥ\\najānatī patiṁ sādhvī\\naśvinau śaraṇaṁ yayau
verses.translation: The chaste and very beautiful Sukanyā could not distinguish her husband from the two Aśvinī-kumāras, for they were equally beautiful. Not understanding who her real husband was, she took shelter of the Aśvinī-kumāras.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nSukanyā could have selected any one of them as her husband, for one could not distinguish among them, but because she was chaste, she took shelter of the Aśvinī-kumāras so that they could inform her who her actual husband was. A chaste woman will never accept any man other than her husband, even if there be someone equally as handsome and qualified.

verses.devanagari: दर्शयित्वा पतिं तस्यै पातिव्रत्येन तोषितौ\\nऋषिमामन्त्र्य ययतुर्विमानेन त्रिविष्टपम ॥१७॥
verses.transliteration: darśayitvā patiṁ tasyai\\npāti-vratyena toṣitau\\nṛṣim āmantrya yayatur\\nvimānena triviṣṭapam
verses.translation: The Aśvinī-kumāras were very pleased to see Sukanyā's chastity and faithfulness. Thus they showed her Cyavana Muni, her husband, and after taking permission from him, they returned to the heavenly planets in their plane.

verses.devanagari: यक्ष्यमाणोऽथ शर्यातिश्च्यवनस्याश्रमं गतः\\nददर्श दुहितुः पार्श्वे पुरुषं सूर्यवर्चसम ॥१८॥
verses.transliteration: yakṣyamāṇo 'tha śaryātiś\\ncyavanasyāśramaṁ gataḥ\\ndadarśa duhituḥ pārśve\\npuruṣaṁ sūrya-varcasam
verses.translation: Thereafter, King Śaryāti, desiring to perform a sacrifice, went to the residence of Cyavana Muni. There he saw by the side of his daughter a very beautiful young man, as bright as the sun.

verses.devanagari: राजा दुहितरं प्राह कृतपादाभिवन्दनाम\\nआशिषश्चाप्रयुञ्जानो नातिप्रीतिमना इव ॥१९॥
verses.transliteration: rājā duhitaraṁ prāha\\nkṛta-pādābhivandanām\\nāśiṣaś cāprayuñjāno\\nnātiprīti-manā iva
verses.translation: After receiving obeisances from his daughter, the King, instead of offering blessings to her, appeared very displeased and spoke as follows.

verses.devanagari: चिकीर्षितं ते किमिदं पतिस्त्वया प्रलम्भितो लोकनमस्कृतो मुनिः\\nयत्त्वं जराग्रस्तमसत्यसम्मतं विहाय जारं भजसेऽमुमध्वगम ॥२०॥
verses.transliteration: cikīrṣitaṁ te kim idaṁ patis tvayā\\npralambhito loka-namaskṛto muniḥ\\nyat tvaṁ jarā-grastam asaty asammataṁ\\nvihāya jāraṁ bhajase 'mum adhvagam
verses.translation: O unchaste girl, what is this that you have desired to do? You have cheated the most respectable husband, who is honored by everyone, for I see that because he was old, diseased and therefore unattractive, you have left his company to accept as your husband this young man, who appears to be a beggar from the street.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This shows the values of Vedic culture. According to the circumstances, Sukanyā had been given a husband who was too old to be compatible with her. Because Cyavana Muni was diseased and very old, he was certainly unfit for the beautiful daughter of King Śaryāti. Nonetheless, her father expected her to be faithful to her husband. When he suddenly saw that his daughter had accepted someone else, even though the man was young and handsome, he immediately chastised her as
asatī,
unchaste, because he assumed that she had accepted another man in the presence of her husband. According to Vedic culture, even if a young woman is given an old husband, she must respectfully serve him. This is chastity. It is not that because she dislikes her husband she may give him up and accept another. This is against Vedic culture. According to Vedic culture, a woman must accept the husband given to her by her parents and remain chaste and faithful to him. Therefore King Śaryāti was surprised to see a young man by the side of Sukanyā.

verses.devanagari: कथं मतिस्तेऽवगतान्यथा सतां कुलप्रसूते कुलदूषणं त्विदम\\nबिभर्षि जारं यदपत्रपा कुलं पितुश्च भर्तुश्च नयस्यधस्तमः ॥२१॥
verses.transliteration: kathaṁ matis te 'vagatānyathā satāṁ\\nkula-prasūte kula-dūṣaṇaṁ tv idam\\nbibharṣi jāraṁ yad apatrapā kulaṁ\\npituś ca bhartuś ca nayasy adhas tamaḥ
verses.translation: O my daughter, who were born in a respectable family, how have you degraded your consciousness in this way? How is it that you are shamelessly maintaining a paramour? You will thus degrade the dynasties of both your father and your husband to hellish life.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
It is quite clear that according to Vedic culture a woman who accepts a paramour or second husband in the presence of the husband she has married is certainly responsible for the degradation of her father's family and the family of her husband. The rules of Vedic culture in this regard are strictly observed in the respectable families of
brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas
and
vaiśyas
even today; only the
śūdras
are degraded in this matter. For a woman of the
brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya
or
vaiśya
class to accept another husband in the presence of the husband she has married, or to file for divorce or accept a boyfriend or paramour, is unacceptable in the Vedic culture. Therefore King Śaryāti, who did not know the real facts of Cyavana Muni's transformation, was surprised to see the behavior of his daughter.

verses.devanagari: एवं ब्रुवाणं पितरं स्मयमाना शुचिस्मिता\\nउवाच तात जामाता तवैष भृगुनन्दनः ॥२२॥
verses.transliteration: evaṁ bruvāṇaṁ pitaraṁ\\nsmayamānā śuci-smitā\\nuvāca tāta jāmātā\\ntavaiṣa bhṛgu-nandanaḥ
verses.translation: Sukanyā, however, being very proud of her chastity, smiled upon hearing the rebukes of her father. She smilingly told him, "My dear father, this young man by my side is your actual son-in-law, the great sage Cyavana, who was born in the family of Bhṛgu."
verses.purport: PURPORT\nAlthough the father chastised the daughter, assuming that she had accepted another husband, the daughter knew that she was completely honest and chaste, and therefore she was smiling. When she explained that her husband, Cyavana Muni, had now been transformed into a young man, she was very proud of her chastity, and thus she smiled as she talked with her father.

verses.devanagari: शशंस पित्रे तत्सर्वं वयोरूपाभिलम्भनम\\nविस्मितः परमप्रीतस्तनयां परिषस्वजे ॥२३॥
verses.transliteration: śaśaṁsa pitre tat sarvaṁ\\nvayo-rūpābhilambhanam\\nvismitaḥ parama-prītas\\ntanayāṁ pariṣasvaje
verses.translation: Thus Sukanyā explained how her husband had received the beautiful body of a young man. When the King heard this he was very surprised, and in great pleasure he embraced his beloved daughter.

verses.devanagari: सोमेन याजयन्वीरं ग्रहं सोमस्य चाग्रहीत\\nअसोमपोरप्यश्विनोश्च्यवनः स्वेन तेजसा ॥२४॥
verses.transliteration: somena yājayan vīraṁ\\ngrahaṁ somasya cāgrahīt\\nasoma-por apy aśvinoś\\ncyavanaḥ svena tejasā
verses.translation: Cyavana Muni, by his own prowess, enabled King Śaryāti to perform the soma-yajña. The muni offered a full pot of soma-rasa to the Aśvinī-kumāras, although they were unfit to drink it.

verses.devanagari: हन्तुं तमाददे वज्रं सद्यो मन्युरमर्षितः\\nसवज्रं स्तम्भयामास भुजमिन्द्रस्य भार्गवः ॥२५॥
verses.transliteration: hantuṁ tam ādade vajraṁ\\nsadyo manyur amarṣitaḥ\\nsavajraṁ stambhayām āsa\\nbhujam indrasya bhārgavaḥ
verses.translation: King Indra, being perturbed and angry, wanted to kill Cyavana Muni, and therefore he impetuously took up his thunderbolt. But Cyavana Muni, by his powers, paralyzed Indra's arm that held the thunderbolt.

verses.devanagari: अन्वजानंस्ततः सर्वे ग्रहं सोमस्य चाश्विनोः\\nभिषजाविति यत्पूर्वं सोमाहुत्या बहिष्कृतौ ॥२६॥
verses.transliteration: anvajānaṁs tataḥ sarve\\ngrahaṁ somasya cāśvinoḥ\\nbhiṣajāv iti yat pūrvaṁ\\nsomāhutyā bahiṣ-kṛtau
verses.translation: Although the Aśvinī-kumāras were only physicians and were therefore excluded from drinking soma-rasa in sacrifices, the demigods agreed to allow them henceforward to drink it.

verses.devanagari: उत्तानबर्हिरानर्तो भूरिषेण इति त्रयः\\nशर्यातेरभवन्पुत्रा आनर्ताद्रेवतोऽभवत ॥२७॥
verses.transliteration: uttānabarhir ānarto\\nbhūriṣeṇa iti trayaḥ\\nśaryāter abhavan putrā\\nānartād revato 'bhavat
verses.translation: King Śaryāti begot three sons, named Uttānabarhi, Ānarta and Bhūriṣeṇa. From Ānarta came a son named Revata.

verses.devanagari: सोऽन्तःसमुद्रे नगरीं विनिर्माय कुशस्थलीम\\nआस्थितोऽभुङ्क्त विषयानानर्तादीनरिन्दम ॥२८॥
verses.transliteration: so 'ntaḥ-samudre nagarīṁ\\nvinirmāya kuśasthalīm\\nāsthito 'bhuṅkta viṣayān\\nānartādīn arindama\\ntasya putra-śataṁ jajñe\\nkakudmi-jyeṣṭham uttamam
verses.translation: O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, subduer of enemies, this Revata constructed a kingdom known as Kuśasthalī in the depths of the ocean. There he lived and ruled such tracts of land as Ānarta, etc. He had one hundred very nice sons, of whom the eldest was Kakudmī.

verses.devanagari: तस्य पुत्रशतं जज्ञए ककुद्मिज्येष्ठमुत्तमम\\nककुद्मी रेवतीं कन्यां स्वामादाय विभुं गतः ॥२९॥
verses.transliteration: kakudmī revatīṁ kanyāṁ\\nsvām ādāya vibhuṁ gataḥ\\nputryā varaṁ paripraṣṭuṁ\\nbrahmalokam apāvṛtam
verses.translation: Taking his own daughter, Revatī, Kakudmī went to Lord Brahmā in Brahmaloka, which is transcendental to the three modes of material nature, and inquired about a husband for her.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
It appears that Brahmaloka, the abode of Lord Brahmā, is also transcendental, above the three modes of material nature (
apāvṛtam
).

verses.devanagari: पुत्र्या वरं परिप्रष्टुं ब्रह्मलोकमपावृतम\\nआवर्तमाने गान्धर्वे स्थितोऽलब्धक्षणः क्षणम ॥३०॥
verses.transliteration: āvartamāne gāndharve\\nsthito 'labdha-kṣaṇaḥ kṣaṇam\\ntad-anta ādyam ānamya\\nsvābhiprāyaṁ nyavedayat
verses.translation: When Kakudmī arrived there, Lord Brahmā was engaged in hearing musical performances by the Gandharvas and had not a moment to talk with him. Therefore Kakudmī waited, and at the end of the musical performances he offered his obeisances to Lord Brahmā and thus submitted his long-standing desire.

verses.devanagari: तदन्त आद्यमानम्य स्वाभिप्रायं न्यवेदयत\\nतच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान्ब्रह्मा प्रहस्य तमुवाच ह ॥३१॥
verses.transliteration: tac chrutvā bhagavān brahmā\\nprahasya tam uvāca ha\\naho rājan niruddhās te\\nkālena hṛdi ye kṛtāḥ
verses.translation: After hearing his words, Lord Brahmā, who is most powerful, laughed loudly and said to Kakudmī: O King, all those whom you may have decided within the core of your heart to accept as your son-in-law have passed away in the course of time.

verses.devanagari: अहो राजन्निरुद्धास्ते कालेन हृदि ये कृताः\\nतत्पुत्रपौत्रनप्त्णां गोत्राणि च न शृण्महे ॥३२॥
verses.transliteration: tat putra-pautra-naptṝṇāṁ\\ngotrāṇi ca na śṛṇmahe\\nkālo 'bhiyātas tri-ṇava-\\ncatur-yuga-vikalpitaḥ
verses.translation: Twenty-seven catur-yugas have already passed. Those upon whom you may have decided are now gone, and so are their sons, grandsons and other descendants. You cannot even hear about their names.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
During Lord Brahmā's day, fourteen Manus or one thousand
mahā-yugas
pass away. Brahmā informed King Kakudmī that twenty-seven
mahā-yugas,
each consisting of the four periods Satya, Tretā, Dvāpara and Kali, had already passed. All the kings and other great personalities born in those
yugas
had now departed from memory into obscurity. This is the way of time as it moves through past, present and future.

verses.devanagari: कालोऽभियातस्त्रिणव चतुर्युगविकल्पितः\\nतद्गच्छ देवदेवांशो बलदेवो महाबलः ॥३३॥
verses.transliteration: tad gaccha deva-devāṁśo\\nbaladevo mahā-balaḥ\\nkanyā-ratnam idaṁ rājan\\nnara-ratnāya dehi bhoḥ
verses.translation: O King, leave here and offer your daughter to Lord Baladeva, who is still present. He is most powerful. Indeed, He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose plenary portion is Lord Viṣṇu. Your daughter is fit to be given to Him in charity.

verses.devanagari: कन्यारत्नमिदं राजन्नररत्नाय देहि भोः\\nभुवो भारावताराय भगवान्भूतभावनः ॥३४॥
verses.transliteration: bhuvo bhārāvatārāya\\nbhagavān bhūta-bhāvanaḥ\\navatīrṇo nijāṁśena\\npuṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ
verses.translation: Lord Baladeva is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. One who hears and chants about Him is purified. Because He is always the well-wisher of all living entities, He has descended with all His paraphernalia to purify the entire world and lessen its burden.

verses.devanagari: अवतीर्णो निजांशेन पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तनः\\nइत्यादिष्टोऽभिवन्द्याजं नृपः स्वपुरमागतः\\nत्यक्तं पुण्यजनत्रासाद्भ्रातृभिर्दिक्ष्ववस्थितैः ॥३५॥
verses.transliteration: ity ādiṣṭo 'bhivandyājaṁ\\nnṛpaḥ sva-puram āgataḥ\\ntyaktaṁ puṇya-jana-trāsād\\nbhrātṛbhir dikṣv avasthitaiḥ
verses.translation: Having received this order from Lord Brahmā, Kakudmī offered obeisances unto him and returned to his own residence. He then saw that his residence was vacant, having been abandoned by his brothers and other relatives, who were living in all directions because of fear of such higher living beings as the Yakṣas.

verses.devanagari: सुतां दत्त्वानवद्याङ्गीं बलाय बलशालिने\\nबदर्याख्यं गतो राजा तप्तुं नारायणाश्रमम ॥३६॥
verses.transliteration: sutāṁ dattvānavadyāṅgīṁ\\nbalāya bala-śāline\\nbadary-ākhyaṁ gato rājā\\ntaptuṁ nārāyaṇāśramam
verses.translation: Thereafter, the King gave his most beautiful daughter in charity to the supremely powerful Baladeva and then retired from worldly life and went to Badarikāśrama to please Nara-Nārāyaṇa.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Thus end the Bhaktivedanta purports of the Ninth Canto, Third Chapter, of the
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,
entitled "The Marriage of Sukanyā and Cyavana Muni."

sections.title: Chapter 4: Ambarīṣa Mahārāja Offended by Durvāsā Muni

verses.devanagari: श्रीशुक उवाच\\nनाभागो नभगापत्यं यं ततं भ्रातरः कविम\\nयविष्ठं व्यभजन्दायं ब्रह्मचारिणमागतम ॥१॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-śuka uvāca\\nnābhāgo nabhagāpatyaṁ\\nyaṁ tataṁ bhrātaraḥ kavim\\nyaviṣṭhaṁ vyabhajan dāyaṁ\\nbrahmacāriṇam āgatam
verses.translation: Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: The son of Nabhaga named Nābhāga lived for a long time at the place of his spiritual master. Therefore, his brothers thought that he was not going to become a gṛhastha and would not return. Consequently, without providing a share for him, they divided the property of their father among themselves. When Nābhāga returned from the place of his spiritual master, they gave him their father as his share.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
There are two kinds of
brahmacārīs.
One may return home, marry and become a householder, whereas the other, known as
bṛhad-vrata,
takes a vow to remain a
brahmacārī
perpetually. The
bṛhad-vrata brahmacārī
does not return from the place of the spiritual master; he stays there, and later he directly takes
sannyāsa.
Because Nābhāga did not return from the place of his spiritual master, his brothers thought that he had taken
bṛhadvrata-brahmacarya.
Therefore, they did not preserve his share, and when he returned they gave him their father as his share.

verses.devanagari: भ्रातरोऽभाङ्क्त किं मह्यं भजाम पितरं तव\\nत्वां ममार्यास्तताभाङ्क्षुर्मा पुत्रक तदादृथाः ॥२॥
verses.transliteration: bhrātaro 'bhāṅkta kiṁ mahyaṁ\\nbhajāma pitaraṁ tava\\ntvāṁ mamāryās tatābhāṅkṣur\\nmā putraka tad ādṛthāḥ
verses.translation: Nābhāga inquired, "My dear brothers, what have you given to me as my share of our father's property?" His elder brothers answered, "We have kept our father as your share." But when Nābhāga went to his father and said, "My dear father, my elder brothers have given you as my share of property," the father replied, "My dear son, do not rely upon their cheating words. I am not your property."

verses.devanagari: इमे अङ्गिरसः सत्रमासतेऽद्य सुमेधसः\\nषष्ठं षष्ठमुपेत्याहः कवे मुह्यन्ति कर्मणि ॥३॥
verses.transliteration: ime aṅgirasaḥ satram\\nāsate 'dya sumedhasaḥ\\nṣaṣṭhaṁ ṣaṣṭham upetyāhaḥ\\nkave muhyanti karmaṇi
verses.translation: Nābhāga's father said: All the descendants of Aṅgirā are now going to perform a great sacrifice, but although they are very intelligent, on every sixth day they will be bewildered in performing sacrifice and will make mistakes in their daily duties.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nNābhāga was very simple hearted. Therefore when he went to his father, the father, in compassion for his son, suggested that as a means of livelihood Nābhāga could go to the descendants of Aṅgirā and take advantage of their misgivings in performing\nyajña.

verses.devanagari: तांस्त्वं शंसय सूक्ते द्वे वैश्वदेवे महात्मनः\\nते स्वर्यन्तो धनं सत्र परिशेषितमात्मनः ॥४॥\\nदास्यन्ति तेऽथ तानर्च्छ तथा स कृतवान्यथा\\nतस्मै दत्त्वा ययुः स्वर्गं ते सत्रपरिशेषणम ॥५॥
verses.transliteration: dāsyanti te 'tha tān arccha\\ntathā sa kṛtavān yathā\\ntasmai dattvā yayuḥ svargaṁ\\nte satra-pariśeṣaṇam
verses.translation: Nābhāga's father continued: "Go to those great souls and describe two Vedic hymns pertaining to Vaiśvadeva. When the great sages have completed the sacrifice and are going to the heavenly planets, they will give you the remnants of the money they have received from the sacrifice. Therefore, go there immediately." Thus Nābhāga acted exactly according to the advice of his father, and the great sages of the Aṅgirā dynasty gave him all their wealth and then went to the heavenly planets.

verses.devanagari: तं कश्चित्स्वीकरिष्यन्तं पुरुषः कृष्णदर्शनः\\nउवाचोत्तरतोऽभ्येत्य ममेदं वास्तुकं वसु ॥६॥
verses.transliteration: taṁ kaścit svīkariṣyantaṁ\\npuruṣaḥ kṛṣṇa-darśanaḥ\\nuvācottarato 'bhyetya\\nmamedaṁ vāstukaṁ vasu
verses.translation: Thereafter, while Nābhāga was accepting the riches, a black-looking person from the north came to him and said, "All the wealth from this sacrificial arena belongs to me."

verses.devanagari: ममेदमृषिभिर्दत्तमिति तर्हि स्म मानवः\\nस्यान्नौ ते पितरि प्रश्नः पृष्टवान्पितरं यथा ॥७॥
verses.transliteration: mamedam ṛṣibhir dattam\\niti tarhi sma mānavaḥ\\nsyān nau te pitari praśnaḥ\\npṛṣṭavān pitaraṁ yathā
verses.translation: Nābhāga then said, "These riches belong to me. The great saintly persons have delivered them to me." When Nābhāga said this, the black-looking person replied, "Let us go to your father and ask him to settle our disagreement." In accordance with this, Nābhāga inquired from his father.

verses.devanagari: यज्ञअवास्तुगतं सर्वमुच्छिष्टमृषयः क्वचित\\nचक्रुर्हि भागं रुद्राय स देवः सर्वमर्हति ॥८॥
verses.transliteration: yajña-vāstu-gataṁ sarvam\\nucchiṣṭam ṛṣayaḥ kvacit\\ncakrur hi bhāgaṁ rudrāya\\nsa devaḥ sarvam arhati
verses.translation: The father of Nābhāga said: Whatever the great sages sacrificed in the arena of the Dakṣa-yajña, they offered to Lord Śiva as his share. Therefore, everything in the sacrificial arena certainly belongs to Lord Śiva.

verses.devanagari: नाभागस्तं प्रणम्याह तवेश किल वास्तुकम\\nइत्याह मे पिता ब्रह्मञ्छिरसा त्वां प्रसादये ॥९॥
verses.transliteration: nābhāgas taṁ praṇamyāha\\ntaveśa kila vāstukam\\nity āha me pitā brahmañ\\nchirasā tvāṁ prasādaye
verses.translation: Thereupon, after offering obeisances to Lord Śiva, Nābhāga said: O worshipable lord, everything in this arena of sacrifice is yours. This is the assertion of my father. Now, with great respect, I bow my head before you, begging your mercy.

verses.devanagari: यत्ते पितावदद्धर्मं त्वं च सत्यं प्रभाषसे\\nददामि ते मन्त्रदृशो ज्ञआनं ब्रह्म सनातनम ॥१०॥
verses.transliteration: yat te pitāvadad dharmaṁ\\ntvaṁ ca satyaṁ prabhāṣase\\ndadāmi te mantra-dṛśo\\njñānaṁ brahma sanātanam
verses.translation: Lord Śiva said: Whatever your father has said is the truth, and you also are speaking the same truth. Therefore, I, who know the Vedic mantras, shall explain transcendental knowledge to you.

verses.devanagari: गृहाण द्रविणं दत्तं मत्सत्रपरिशेषितम\\nइत्युक्त्वान्तर्हितो रुद्रो भगवान्धर्मवत्सलः ॥११॥
verses.transliteration: gṛhāṇa draviṇaṁ dattaṁ\\nmat-satra-pariśeṣitam\\nity uktvāntarhito rudro\\nbhagavān dharma-vatsalaḥ
verses.translation: Lord Śiva said, "Now you may take all the wealth remaining from the sacrifice, for I give it to you." After saying this, Lord Śiva, who is most adherent to the religious principles, disappeared from that place.

verses.devanagari: य एतत्संस्मरेत्प्रातः सायं च सुसमाहितः\\nकविर्भवति मन्त्रज्ञओ गतिं चैव तथात्मनः ॥१२॥
verses.transliteration: ya etat saṁsmaret prātaḥ\\nsāyaṁ ca susamāhitaḥ\\nkavir bhavati mantra-jño\\ngatiṁ caiva tathātmanaḥ
verses.translation: If one hears and chants or remembers this narration in the morning and evening with great attention, he certainly becomes learned, experienced in understanding the Vedic hymns, and expert in self-realization.

verses.devanagari: नाभागादम्बरीषोऽभून्महाभागवतः कृती\\nनास्पृशद्ब्रह्मशापोऽपि यं न प्रतिहतः क्वचित ॥१३॥
verses.transliteration: nābhāgād ambarīṣo 'bhūn\\nmahā-bhāgavataḥ kṛtī\\nnāspṛśad brahma-śāpo 'pi\\nyaṁ na pratihataḥ kvacit
verses.translation: From Nābhāga, Mahārāja Ambarīṣa took birth. Mahārāja Ambarīṣa was an exalted devotee, celebrated for his great merits. Although he was cursed by an infallible brāhmaṇa, the curse could not touch him.

verses.devanagari: श्रीराजोवाच\\nभगवन्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि राजर्षेस्तस्य धीमतः\\nन प्राभूद्यत्र निर्मुक्तो ब्रह्मदण्डो दुरत्ययः ॥१४॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rājovāca\\nbhagavañ chrotum icchāmi\\nrājarṣes tasya dhīmataḥ\\nna prābhūd yatra nirmukto\\nbrahma-daṇḍo duratyayaḥ
verses.translation: King Parīkṣit inquired: O great personality, Mahārāja Ambarīṣa was certainly most exalted and meritorious in character. I wish to hear about him. How surprising it is that the curse of a brāhmaṇa, which is insurmountable, could not act upon him.

verses.devanagari: श्रीशुक उवाच\\nअम्बरीषो महाभागः सप्तद्वीपवतीं महीम\\nअव्ययां च श्रियं लब्ध्वा विभवं चातुलं भुवि ॥१५॥\\nमेनेऽतिदुर्लभं पुंसां सर्वं तत्स्वप्नसंस्तुतम\\nविद्वान्विभवनिर्वाणं तमो विशति यत्पुमान ॥१६॥
verses.transliteration: mene 'tidurlabhaṁ puṁsāṁ\\nsarvaṁ tat svapna-saṁstutam\\nvidvān vibhava-nirvāṇaṁ\\ntamo viśati yat pumān
verses.translation: Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Mahārāja Ambarīṣa, the most fortunate personality, achieved the rule of the entire world, consisting of seven islands, and achieved inexhaustible, unlimited opulence and prosperity on earth. Although such a position is rarely obtained, Mahārāja Ambarīṣa did not care for it at all, for he knew very well that all such opulence is material. Like that which is imagined in a dream, such opulence will ultimately be destroyed. The King knew that any nondevotee who attains such opulence merges increasingly into material nature's mode of darkness.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nFor a devotee material opulence is insignificant, whereas for a nondevotee material opulence is the cause of increasing bondage, for a devotee knows that anything material is temporary, whereas a nondevotee regards the temporary so-called happiness as everything and forgets the path of self-realization. Thus for the nondevotee material opulence is a disqualification for spiritual advancement.

verses.devanagari: वासुदेवे भगवति तद्भक्तेषु च साधुषु\\nप्राप्तो भावं परं विश्वं येनेदं लोष्ट्रवत्स्मृतम ॥१७॥
verses.transliteration: vāsudeve bhagavati\\ntad-bhakteṣu ca sādhuṣu\\nprāpto bhāvaṁ paraṁ viśvaṁ\\nyenedaṁ loṣṭravat smṛtam
verses.translation: Mahārāja Ambarīṣa was a great devotee of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vāsudeva, and of the saintly persons who are the Lord's devotees. Because of this devotion, he thought of the entire universe as being as insignificant as a piece of stone.

verses.devanagari: स वै मनः कृष्णपदारविन्दयोर्वचांसि वैकुण्ठगुणानुवर्णने\\nकरौ हरेर्मन्दिरमार्जनादिषु श्रुतिं चकाराच्युतसत्कथोदये ॥१८॥\\nमुकुन्दलिङ्गालयदर्शने दृशौ तद्भृत्यगात्रस्पर्शेऽङ्गसङ्गमम\\nघ्राणं च तत्पादसरोजसौरभे श्रीमत्तुलस्या रसनां तदर्पिते ॥१९॥\\nपादौ हरेः क्षेत्रपदानुसर्पणे शिरो हृषीकेशपदाभिवन्दने\\nकामं च दास्ये न तु कामकाम्यया यथोत्तमश्लोकजनाश्रया रतिः ॥२०॥
verses.transliteration: pādau hareḥ kṣetra-padānusarpaṇe\\nśiro hṛṣīkeśa-padābhivandane\\nkāmaṁ ca dāsye na tu kāma-kāmyayā\\nyathottamaśloka-janāśrayā ratiḥ
verses.translation: Mahārāja Ambarīṣa always engaged his mind in meditating upon the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, his words in describing the glories of the Lord, his hands in cleansing the Lord's temple, and his ears in hearing the words spoken by Kṛṣṇa or about Kṛṣṇa. He engaged his eyes in seeing the Deity of Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa's temples and Kṛṣṇa's places like Mathurā and Vṛndāvana, he engaged his sense of touch in touching the bodies of the Lord's devotees, he engaged his sense of smell in smelling the fragrance of tulasī offered to the Lord, and he engaged his tongue in tasting the Lord's prasāda. He engaged his legs in walking to the holy places and temples of the Lord, his head in bowing down before the Lord, and all his desires in serving the Lord, twenty-four hours a day. Indeed, Mahārāja Ambarīṣa never desired anything for his own sense gratification. He engaged all his senses in devotional service, in various engagements related to the Lord. This is the way to increase attachment for the Lord and be completely free from all material desires.
